sections.heading: Understanding CBC teacher training in the Kenyan CBE context
sections.body: Identify professional learning areas and ways to verify current TSC and Ministry requirements. Begin with the exact grade, learning area and school context. The curriculum design explains the intended learning outcomes; school-level plans should translate those outcomes into realistic learning experiences, resources and evidence of progress. Avoid relying on undated templates or social-media summaries when an official design or circular is available.

sections.heading: A practical implementation approach
sections.body: Teachers can begin by reviewing the relevant KICD curriculum design, identifying the expected outcome and deciding what learners will do to demonstrate it. Parents should understand the learning purpose and provide reasonable support at home. School leaders should make time, materials and professional collaboration available. Learners should be given clear instructions, opportunities to practise and feedback they can act on.

sections.heading: Common implementation mistakes to avoid
sections.body: Do not treat a template as proof that learning has taken place, copy another grade's requirements without checking, or assume every school has identical staffing and facilities. Avoid assessment tasks that reward expensive materials or adult assistance rather than the learner's own understanding. Keep records accurate, accessible and proportionate to their purpose.

sections.heading: Planning checklist and official verification
sections.body: Before implementation, confirm the current curriculum design, grade and learning area; identify the outcome and assessment evidence; check resource and accessibility needs; communicate expectations to learners and parents; and review progress after the activity. Verify curriculum information with KICD, policy and implementation circulars with the Ministry of Education, assessment information with KNEC and teacher professional requirements with TSC.

faqs.question: What is the most important starting point for CBC teacher training?
faqs.answer: Start with the current curriculum design and the specific grade or learning area. Identify the intended learning outcome before choosing a template, activity or assessment method.

faqs.question: Where can Kenyan schools verify current CBC/CBE guidance?
faqs.answer: Use KICD for curriculum designs and approved learning materials, the Ministry of Education for policy and implementation circulars, KNEC for national assessment information and TSC for teacher professional requirements.

faqs.question: Can a school use the same plan for every grade?
faqs.answer: No. Adapt plans to the grade, learning area, learner needs, school context and current official guidance. A generic template should never replace the relevant curriculum design.

intro: Teach teachers to navigate curriculum design documents and turn outcomes into lesson and assessment plans. This guide is designed for Kenyan teacher planning and schemes readers and connects practical school-level decisions with the current official curriculum framework. sections.heading: Read the introductory guidance first
sections.body: Check the level, grade and learning area, then read the rationale, level learning outcomes and any notes explaining the curriculum structure. This prevents isolated copying of a table without understanding its context.

sections.heading: Follow the strand and sub-strand structure
sections.body: Strands organise broad areas of learning; sub-strands break them into more specific content areas. Use the sequence in the design to understand how learning develops across the grade.

sections.heading: Interpret specific learning outcomes
sections.body: Look closely at the action words and expected learner performance. Outcomes should guide what learners will demonstrate, not just what a teacher will cover or dictate.

sections.heading: Translate the design into classroom planning
sections.body: Use the suggested learning experiences to plan schemes and lessons, then select assessment evidence that shows whether the outcome has been achieved. Adapt the activity to the class while retaining the intended learning.
